AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.summary: Mathlib already has the real-variable toolkit this roadmap asks for: the Schwartz space and Fourier transform on real inner-product spaces, Fourier inversion, Poisson summation for ℤ ⊂ ℝ, Mellin transforms with inversion, and differentiation under the integral. It also has Deligne's Γ_ℝ/Γ_ℂ, finite-ring Gauss sums and Dirichlet conductors, and the GL₁/ℚ global theory in classical theta–Mellin form (continuation, functional equation with Gauss-sum root number, Euler product, trivial-character pole, removal of Euler factors by change of level), as well as Hecke's continuation and functional-equation package for holomorphic cusp forms on arithmetic subgroups, which is the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case. Tau Ceti adds the discreteness of K in 𝔸_K, ideal-indexed Euler products over number fields, and Shimura's Hecke-ring structure for GL₂ (the polynomial p-local Hecke ring and the prime-power recurrence). Everything local-field-theoretic and adelic is missing: Schwartz–Bruhat spaces at finite places, standard additive characters and self-dual measures, adelic Poisson summation, Tate local zeta integrals and ε-factors, Hecke L-functions beyond ℚ, and all of Godement–Jacquet, Rankin–Selberg, Satake/L-group Euler factors and the interpolation interfaces. Neither library has smooth admissible representations of p-adic groups.

targets.target: local Schwartz–Bruhat spaces: locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places, Schwartz functions at real and complex places
targets.note: `SchwartzMap` (𝓢(E,F) on a real normed space) covers the archimedean places ℝ and ℂ ≅ ℝ². Neither library packages locally constant compactly supported functions on a nonarchimedean local field as a space; searches for Schwartz–Bruhat/Bruhat–Schwartz and for `LocallyConstant` with `HasCompactSupport` found nothing.

targets.target: Fourier transform on local fields with respect to a nontrivial additive character; self-duality of the local additive groups
targets.note: `Fourier.fourierIntegral e μ f` is defined for any commutative ring with a unitary character `AddChar 𝕜 Circle` and a measure, so a local-field transform can be written, but only the real inner-product-space case has theorems. No standard character x ↦ exp(2πi{Tr x}_p) of ℚ_p or its extensions, no self-dual Haar measure and no isomorphism F_v ≅ F_v^ exist. `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/AddChar.lean` classifies p-adic-valued characters of ℤ_p (Amice), a different object. Tau Ceti classifies continuous characters of the circle only.

targets.target: restricted tensor-product adelic Schwartz–Bruhat space S(𝔸_F) = ⊗'_v S(F_v)
targets.note: The restricted product and 𝔸_K exist as topological rings. There is no restricted tensor product of local function spaces and no space of factorizable adelic test functions; searches for restricted tensor products found nothing in either library.

targets.target: Fourier inversion (local and adelic, including the reflected argument)
targets.note: Inversion is proved on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with the 2π convention, for integrable f with integrable 𝓕f (continuous or at continuity points). This covers the real and complex places; nothing covers nonarchimedean fields or 𝔸_F.

targets.target: change-of-character and change-of-measure formulas for local and adelic Fourier transforms
targets.note: Proved covariances are translation and linear isometries on real spaces, and Tau Ceti converts between the 2π Fourier convention and Mathlib's characteristic-function convention on real inner-product spaces. There is no formula relating the transforms for ψ and ψ(a·), and no rescaling of self-dual measures.

targets.target: adelic Poisson summation for the diagonal lattice F ⊂ 𝔸_F, with the volume of 𝔸_F/F
targets.note: Poisson summation is proved only for ℤ ⊂ ℝ: for continuous f with locally uniform summability of translates, and for Schwartz f. Tau Ceti proves K discrete and closed in 𝔸_K. Compactness of 𝔸_K/K (only mentioned in that file's docstring), its covolume, and any lattice or adelic Poisson formula are absent.

targets.target: holomorphic parameter integrals, Mellin transforms and the domination estimates that justify differentiating under the integral
targets.note: Differentiation of parametric integrals over any `RCLike` field (so holomorphic dependence), the Mellin transform on (0,∞) with convergence and holomorphy in s from rpow bounds, and Mellin inversion are all proved. They are real-line tools: no Mellin transform over F_v^× for finite v or over the idele class group is defined.

duplicates.note: Also builds adelic test functions as restricted tensor products of locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places (with C_c^∞ rather than Schwartz functions at infinity), so there should be a single restricted-tensor-product construction.

Defines the adelic Weil representation on the restricted tensor product of local Schwartz spaces and proves compatibility with changes of additive character, the same space and change-of-character formulas as AL.0.
The global-function-field counterpart: self-dual local characters and Haar measures from a differential, the residue pairing, discreteness and cocompactness of K ⊂ 𝔸_K, and adelic Poisson summation.
Also plans Mellin transforms and convergence proofs for interchanging limits, differentiation and Euler products, the analytic tools of AL.0's last sentence.

Declared supplier rather than overlap: it states discreteness of K in 𝔸_K and compactness of 𝔸_K/K, the lattice and covolume that AL.0's Poisson summation takes from GlobalNumberFields. Discreteness is already proved in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: local Tate zeta integral Z(f,χ,s) = ∫ f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a quasi-character χ of F_v^× and a Schwartz–Bruhat f, convergent for Re s > 0
targets.note: At a real place and on ℝ_{>0}, the integral is Mathlib's Mellin transform, and ∫_0^∞ t^{a−1}e^{−rt} dt = r^{−a}Γ(a) is proved. There are no quasi-characters of F_v^× as objects, no multiplicative Haar measure d×x on a local field, and no nonarchimedean zeta integral.

targets.target: rationality of the nonarchimedean zeta integrals in q_v^{−s}
targets.note: No nonarchimedean zeta integral exists to be rational. Mathlib's `ofPowerSeries q f` only turns a formal power series in T = q^{−s} into a formal Dirichlet series.

targets.target: meromorphic continuation of the archimedean zeta integrals
targets.note: Continuation is available for Γ (hence for the Gaussian integral Γ_ℝ) and, abstractly, for Mellin transforms of Mathlib's weak FE-pairs (constant plus rapid decay, with f(1/x) = εx^k g(x)). There is no continuation of ∫_{ℝ^×} f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a general Schwartz f by Taylor expansion at 0, and no ℂ^× version.

targets.target: L-, ε- and γ-factors with exact normalizations and the local functional equation
targets.note: No local ε- or γ-factor and no local functional equation exist. `rootNumber` is the global root number of a Dirichlet character (Gauss sum over ZMod N divided by i^a√N), `gammaFactor` its archimedean factor, and the Γ_ℝ reflection identities are archimedean γ-factor ratios. None is obtained from a local integral.

targets.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
targets.note: Deligne's archimedean factors are in Mathlib with their doubling and reflection formulas, poles and residues. They are identified with the Mellin transform of a Gaussian theta sum (`hasSum_mellin_pi_mul_sq`), but not as the local zeta integral of the Gaussian against a character of ℝ^×.

targets.target: unramified and ramified characters of F_v^×, conductor exponents, Gauss sums and character twists
targets.note: Mathlib has Gauss sums over finite rings, with g(χ)g(χ⁻¹) = χ(−1)#R for nontrivial χ on a finite field, and conductors and primitive characters of Dirichlet characters. There is no unramified/ramified decomposition of characters of ℚ_p^× or K_v^×, no conductor exponent a(χ_v), and no local Gauss sum of a ramified character against ψ_v. Tau Ceti has only ring conductors (e.g. the conductor exponent of an order), not character conductors.

targets.target: global zeta integral: Euler factorization, meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Hecke L-functions via Poisson summation, keeping the trivial-character poles
targets.note: For F = ℚ and finite-order characters, Mathlib proves continuation, the functional equation with conductor, Gauss-sum root number and parity, the Euler product and the residue of the trivial character. It uses the classical Hurwitz/theta–Mellin route (with `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` for ζ), not idelic integrals. Over a general number field there is only the Dedekind zeta series with its residue as a one-sided real limit (Mathlib) and its Euler product for Re s > 1 (Tau Ceti). No continuation or functional equation of Dedekind zeta or Hecke L-functions exists, and no idelic zeta integral.

duplicates.note: Continuation, functional equations with conductor, Gauss sum and parity, gamma factors and the principal-character pole for ζ and Dirichlet L-functions: the F = ℚ finite-order case of AL.1's global statements, which Mathlib largely has.
Completed Hecke and Dedekind L-functions over number fields with real/complex gamma factors, residues and ramified Euler factors, the same global targets as AL.1.

Defines Hecke characters as continuous characters of the idele class group, with local components, finite conductor and unitary part: the character carriers and conductors that AL.1 computes local factors for.
Classifies the continuous characters of ℝ^× and ℂ^× as |x|^s sgn(x)^ε and (z/|z|)^k|z|^s, the archimedean quasi-characters whose zeta integrals produce AL.1's real and complex gamma factors.

Proves Mellin-transform continuation, primitive-character Gauss sums, conductor change and imprimitive Euler-factor deletion, and the Dedekind-zeta pole, which it attributes to AL.1's trivial-character Tate theorem. These overlap AL.1's Dirichlet-character and trivial-character targets.
Proves the GL₁ dictionary with Hecke characters, including infinity type, conductor and unitary twist: the same character bookkeeping AL.1 does locally.

targets.target: local Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals from Schwartz(–Bruhat) functions on M_n(E) and matrix coefficients of irreducible admissible representations of GL_n(E)
targets.note: Neither library has smooth or admissible representations of GL_n over a local field or their matrix coefficients; searches for admissible/smooth representation, matrix coefficient, Godement and Jacquet found nothing relevant. Only abstract Haar measure on locally compact groups and Schwartz functions on real vector spaces are available.

targets.target: nonarchimedean rationality in q^{−s}, the fractional-ideal characterization of L(s,π) and the local functional equation with γ(s,π,ψ)
targets.note: Nothing: no local zeta integrals, no fractional ideal of ℂ[q^{±s}] and no ε-factors for GL_n.

targets.target: archimedean gamma factors via Casselman–Wallach globalizations, Schwartz estimates and meromorphic parameter integrals; their functional equation
targets.note: No (g,K)-modules, Harish-Chandra modules or smooth Fréchet globalizations exist in either library (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 owns them).

targets.target: unramified spherical computation L(s,π) = det(1 − q^{−s}A_π)^{−1} and comparison with the Satake parameter
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Shimura's Theorem 3.20 for n = 2 (and n = 1): the p-local Hecke ring of GL_n over ℚ relative to GL_n(ℤ) is a polynomial ring on the diagonal double cosets. It also proves the GL₂ recurrence T(p^{k+1}) = T(p)T(p^k) − p·T(p,p)T(p^{k−1}), the formal identity behind the degree-two Euler factor. There is no spherical function, Satake transform, unramified principal series or local zeta integral.

targets.target: global integral for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n: Euler factorization, analytic continuation and functional equation, with the n = 1 pole separated
targets.note: Only classical special cases exist, proved by Hecke's Mellin argument rather than adelic integrals. For n = 2 over ℚ and holomorphic modular forms on an arithmetic subgroup, Mathlib packages f(it) and its S-translate as a weak FE-pair (continuation and a functional equation relating f to f|S) and proves cusp-form L-functions entire; Tau Ceti identifies the coefficient L-series with them (`CuspForm.hasEntireExtension_qExpansion_coeff`). For a newform, Tau Ceti proves the formal Euler factorization at primes not dividing the level: a_{mn} = a_m a_n for coprime good m, n, and a_{p^{r+2}} = a_p a_{p^{r+1}} − χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{p^r}. The analytic Euler product is not stated. For n = 1 over ℚ there are Dirichlet L-functions. Nothing exists for n ≥ 3, for Maass forms or over other number fields.

targets.target: bounds and normalization conversions for use in interpolation formulas
targets.note: No GL_n local-factor normalizations exist to convert between.

duplicates.note: Relates the GL_n Hecke polynomial P_v(X) to the normalized Satake transform, determinant character and Tate twist: the unramified comparison AL.2 derives from the spherical zeta integral, so the two normalization dictionaries must coincide.

Hecke's completed L-function and functional equation for newforms of level N with the Atkin–Lehner sign, and their Euler product: the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case of AL.2's global Euler factorization and functional equation.

Constructs local constants for GL_m on the analytic side and proves their dictionary with Weil–Deligne constants. Its text assigns the integral constructions to AL, so its analytic L/ε-factors must be AL.2's rather than a second construction.

targets.target: comparison of the nonarchimedean Whittaker/derivative constructions of SR.5 with the classical complex Whittaker model
targets.note: No Whittaker functional, Kirillov model or Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivative exists in either library; the word Whittaker occurs only in bibliography entries for Whittaker–Watson.

targets.target: GL_n × GL_m local Rankin–Selberg integrals: convergence, nonarchimedean rationality and gcd-normalized L-factors
targets.note: Nothing. Searches for Rankin–Selberg, Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika and gcd L-factors found nothing; Tau Ceti's only 'Rankin' is Rankin's trick in an ideal-counting bound.

targets.target: archimedean Whittaker functionals with uniqueness and continuity on Casselman–Wallach globalizations, completed tensor products, and Jacquet's estimates (§§2–16)
targets.note: Mathlib has the injective seminorm on finite tensor products of normed spaces, but no completed projective tensor product of Fréchet spaces, no globalization and no Whittaker functional.

targets.target: archimedean holomorphic multiples, boundedness in vertical strips, gamma factors and functional equation without a gcd argument
targets.note: Only the general Phragmén–Lindelöf principle in a vertical strip is available as a tool; no Rankin–Selberg integral exists to apply it to.

targets.target: unramified computations, global unfolding for cuspidal data, poles in the contragredient/twist case and nonvanishing in the proved regions
targets.note: Mathlib defines only the Petersson integrand y^k f(τ)·conj f'(τ); there is no unfolding of an Eisenstein series against cusp forms and no Rankin–Selberg L-function.

targets.target: comparison of integral rational structures, Gauss sums and complex periods with the cohomological normalization; periods up to their scalar ambiguity
targets.note: Finite-ring Gauss sums exist, but there is no period of an automorphic representation, no cohomological normalization and no rational structure to compare.

duplicates.note: Defines period lines and scalar periods Ω_f^± of a newform up to basis choice, with Gauss sums and critical values of twists: the GL₂ × GL₁ case of AL.3's period comparison and scalar-ambiguity requirement.
Proves a Rankin–Selberg/Hecke evaluation of the regulator integral for modular units at a stated level and character, a specific GL₂ × GL₂ unfolding that should consume AL.3 rather than reprove it.

Declared supplier: builds the Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and Whittaker functionals AL.3 imports. The comparison with the classical complex Whittaker model sits on the boundary and should have one owner.

targets.target: Euler polynomial det(1 − r(t_v)X) attached to the Satake semisimple conjugacy class t_v and an algebraic representation r of the L-group
targets.note: `Matrix.charpolyRev M = det(1 − X·M)` supplies the polynomial once a matrix is given. No L-group, no Satake class and no representation of a dual group exist in either library; searches for Satake, L-group, Langlands dual and dual group found nothing.

targets.target: invariance of the Euler polynomial under conjugacy, direct sum, tensor product, duality and scalar extension
targets.note: The linear algebra for conjugacy, direct sums and base change is in Mathlib for characteristic polynomials (hence for their reverses). There is no formula for the characteristic polynomial of a tensor product or of the contragredient in terms of the factors, and nothing ties these to Satake parameters.

targets.target: partial Euler product L^S(s,π,r) and its convergence under a supplied bound on the Satake eigenvalues
targets.note: Mathlib builds formal L-functions from local power series in q^{−s} (`ofPowerSeries`, `eulerProduct`) and proves ∏_p Σ_e f(p^e) = Σ f(n) for multiplicative f with absolutely summable values. Tau Ceti has the ideal-indexed Euler product of a multiplicative weight over a number field, and the degree-two good-prime recurrence of newform coefficients (the standard L-function of GL₂/ℚ in formal form). The step from an eigenvalue bound |α_{v,i}| ≤ q_v^θ to absolute convergence of a degree-n Euler product for Re s > 1 + θ is not proved, and no L^S(s,π,r) is defined.

targets.target: comparison with the AL.1–AL.3 factors and with Weil–Deligne L-factors under an actual local-compatibility theorem
targets.note: No Weil group, Weil–Deligne representation or local L-factor of a Galois representation exists in either library, and no AL.1–AL.3 factors exist to compare.

duplicates.note: For GL_n and its standard representation, constructs the Hecke polynomial Σ(−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}T_{v,i}X^{n−i} and relates it to normalized Satake: the same unramified Euler polynomial as AL.4 in that case.
Builds the normalization dictionary among normalized Satake, the integral Hecke polynomial, Frobenius conventions and Tate twists, the conventions AL.4's Euler polynomials must follow.
Defines completed L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data, the Galois-side factors AL.4 is to compare with.

targets.target: removal and reinsertion of Euler factors at a finite set, and imprimitive/primitive comparisons
targets.note: For Dirichlet characters Mathlib proves L(χ at level N, s) = L(χ, s)·∏_{p∣N}(1 − χ(p)p^{−s}) as entire or meromorphic functions, and identifies a character with the change of level of its primitive character. Tau Ceti restricts ideal weights away from a finite set of primes and proves finite Euler products for the supported part. Nothing exists for GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions.

targets.target: critical-value normalization, functional-equation sign and algebraicity inputs for the GL₂ and Rankin families of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions
targets.note: Only GL₁/ℚ analogues exist: rationality of ζ(−k) via Bernoulli numbers and the root number of a Dirichlet character. No critical values, periods or signs of GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions are formalized.

targets.target: compatibility of conductor exponents, local test vectors and character twists
targets.note: No local conductor exponent of a representation, no newvector or test vector, and no twisting of local representations exists.

targets.target: explicit limiting or derivative results for vanishing Euler factors (exceptional zeros), without cancellation
targets.note: Nothing on exceptional zeros or L-invariants in either library.

targets.target: export of the formulas both as formal local polynomials and as complex evaluations
targets.note: Mathlib's route from local polynomials, through `PowerSeries.invOfUnit` and `ofPowerSeries`/`eulerProduct`, to `LSeries` provides the formal-versus-complex carriers. The GL₂ and Rankin formulas to export do not exist.

duplicates.note: Proves conductor change, imprimitive Euler-factor deletion and algebraicity of the complex values for Dirichlet characters: AL.5's removal/reinsertion and algebraicity interfaces for GL₁.
Primitive/imprimitive comparisons, conductor change and the interpolation formula with its removed Euler factor (1 − (χη)(p)p^{k−1}), the GL₁ instance of AL.5's contracts.
Proves changes of periods, coefficients and primitive/imprimitive conventions across the p-adic constructions, the consumer-side twin of AL.5's normalization interfaces.
States the GL₂ interpolation formula with its Euler factor (1 − χ(p)p^j/α), Gauss sum, (2πi)^{j+1} and period normalization, the critical-value normalization AL.5 is to supply.
Formulates normalized critical values with signs and powers of 2πi and retains ramified and imprimitive corrections: the same normalization targets from the periods side.
